data.value: Visitors whose browsers run JavaScript give a post one reaction (Like, Love, Thanks, Insightful or Funny) and can change or remove it; posts show the reactions given with their counts. Nobody signs in: a browser remembers its own reaction, and the server counts at most one per post per day from an address and browser, through a hash that changes daily. The analytics show the reactions. Turned off, they go from the posts; the counts are kept.

data.name: ReactedPostsCaption
data.value: The posts with the most reactions, by reaction

data.name: ReactionsOff
data.value: Reactions are turned off in Site settings.

data.name: CommentsHelp
data.value: Posts get a comment form, for visitors whose browsers run JavaScript, and show approved comments under the text. Visitors' comments and edits wait under Comments until an editor approves them: admins moderate every post's comments, authors their own posts'. An editor's own comment on a post they moderate appears at once. Moderators get an hourly digest of what waits (with email set up). Visitors don't sign in: the writer's browser keeps a key to edit or delete their comment. A post can close its own comments. Turned off, the form and the comments go; they're kept.

data.name: CloseCommentsHelp
data.value: The form goes; comments already approved stay.
